clause_analysis.title: Payment
clause_analysis.original_clause: 9. STATEMENTS AND PAYMENTS. Law Firm will send Client monthly statements indicating attorneys' fees and costs incurred and their basis, and any current balance owed. Any balance will be due and payable in full within 15 days after the statement is mailed. Client agrees that Law Firm may elect to close Client's file and stop work on the file if the account is not paid in full within 15 days after the billing date, unless special arrangements are agreed upon by Law Firm and Client and confirmed in writing. Law Firm shall have a lien for services rendered and costs advanced on any sums recovered, whether by settlement or judgment, on account of the claims of Client. Law Firm's lien shall also cover any additional charges and/or costs related to Client's account such as Law Firm's costs of collection of a past due account owed by Client to Law Firm and any service charge on Client's delinquent balance.
clause_analysis.reason: The broad lien or payment security clause may be overly broad and potentially violate professional conduct rules, as it includes costs of collection and service charges without clear limits or prior written notice.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the clause to limit the lien to undisputed earned fees and reasonable costs, subject to applicable professional rules and a fair dispute process.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider negotiating a clear definition of 'reasonable costs' and 'undisputed earned fees' with the Law Firm, as well as a process for resolving disputes over the lien, to ensure a fair and transparent payment process.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 9. STATEMENTS AND PAYMENTS. Law Firm will send Client monthly statements indicating attorneys' fees and costs incurred and their basis, and any current balance owed. Any balance will be due and payable in full within 15 days after the statement is mailed. Client agrees that Law Firm may elect to close Client's file and stop work on the file if the account is not paid in full within 15 days after the billing date, unless special arrangements are agreed upon by Law Firm and Client and confirmed in writing. Law Firm shall have a lien for services rendered and costs advanced on any sums recovered, whether by settlement or judgment, on account of the claims of Client, limited to undisputed earned fees and reasonable costs as defined by applicable professional rules. Law Firm's lien shall also cover any additional charges and/or costs related to Client's account such as Law Firm's costs of collection of a past due account owed by Client to Law Firm, subject to prior written notice and a fair dispute process.

clause_analysis.title: Payment
clause_analysis.issue_identified: Uncapped collection costs or service charge
clause_analysis.original_clause: 10. DELINQUENT ACCOUNTS. In the event that Client does not pay his or her account in full when it becomes due, Client agrees to pay all costs of collection plus a service charge on any delinquent balance at the rate of ______.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause is uncertain and may lead to excessive collection costs or service charges, which could be detrimental to the Client.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate with the Law Firm to cap the collection costs and service charge at a reasonable rate, such as 15% of the delinquent balance, and provide prior written notice to the Client.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider proposing a compromise on the collection costs and service charge, and request that the Law Firm provide a detailed breakdown of the costs and a clear explanation of the service charge calculation.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 10. DELINQUENT ACCOUNTS. In the event that Client does not pay his or her account in full when it becomes due, Client agrees to pay all costs of collection plus a service charge on any delinquent balance at the rate of 15% per annum, with prior written notice to Client. The service charge shall not exceed the actual costs of collection, and Client shall be provided with a detailed breakdown of the costs and a clear explanation of the service charge calculation.

clause_analysis.title: Document Retention
clause_analysis.issue_identified: Law Firm will destroy Client's file without notifying Client
clause_analysis.original_clause: 20. DOCUMENT RETENTION. It is Law Firm's policy to retain Client's file in Law Firm's storage facility for a period of not more than seven (7) years. Thereafter, Law Firm will ultimately destroy all files, documents, records, and writings related to each engagement for which Law Firm has been retained without notifying Client of the destruction of these items. Therefore, to be certain that Law Firm has not retained any material that Client may need or desire, Law Firm will return to Client all original documents Client has made available to Law Firm if Client so instructs Law Firm in writing within thirty (30) days after Law Firm mails to Client a letter informing Client that Law Firm has completed the services agreed to be provided under this agreement. After the thirty (30) day period has expired, Law Firm will charge a $25.00 fee for obtaining Client's file from Law Firm's storage facility. Law Firm will not obtain Client's file from its storage facility until such sum has been received by Law Firm.
clause_analysis.reason: The Law Firm's policy to destroy Client's file without notifying Client may violate professional conduct obligations and potentially breach confidentiality.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised clause that requires the Law Firm to provide Client with prior written notice and an opportunity to retrieve their file before destruction.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of transparency and Client control over their file, and highlight the potential risks of non-compliance with professional conduct obligations and confidentiality requirements.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 20. DOCUMENT RETENTION. It is Law Firm's policy to retain Client's file in Law Firm's storage facility for a period of not more than seven (7) years. Thereafter, Law Firm will provide Client with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice before destroying any files, documents, records, and writings related to each engagement for which Law Firm has been retained. During this notice period, Client may request in writing that Law Firm return to Client all original documents Client has made available to Law Firm. If Client so instructs Law Firm in writing, Law Firm will return to Client all original documents within ten (10) business days after receipt of Client's request. After the notice period has expired, Law Firm will charge a $25.00 fee for obtaining Client's file from Law Firm's storage facility, but only if Client has not retrieved their file during the notice period.

clause_analysis.title: Confidentiality / Privilege
clause_analysis.original_clause: Of course, should either of you feel for any reason that you need the advice of another attorney regarding any aspect of the services we provide for you, each of you should feel free to obtain his or her own attorney to provide advice and counsel on this matter, and to assure you that our representation of one of you is not adversely influenced by our representation of the other. Anything that either of you communicate to us will be fully and freely disclosed to the other, and no information will be kept confidential as between the two of you. Should the two of you ever become involved in any lawsuit against one another, neither of you will be able to invoke the lawyer-client privilege as to any communication made by or to us in the course of our joint representation of you, and either of you may compel us to testify in court as to any communication made in the course of that representation. We have no reason to expect that any of these problems will actually arise in your case. Nevertheless, the ethical rules governing the conduct of lawyers require that we explain to you the problems that could arise if we represent each of you at the same time, and that we obtain your consent to this joint representation. We have explained these possible problems and the potential advantages of separate counsel to you.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause waives the lawyer-client privilege and confidentiality between the parties, potentially exposing sensitive information and compromising the attorney-client relationship.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the clause to ensure that it complies with applicable laws and regulations, and that the waiver of privilege and confidentiality is clearly disclosed and consented to by both parties.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate a clear and specific waiver of privilege and confidentiality that is limited to the joint representation and does not expose sensitive information. Ensure that the waiver is informed and consented to by both parties, and that the consequences of waiving privilege and confidentiality are clearly disclosed.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: In any joint representation, Law Firm shall explain in writing the confidentiality and privilege consequences of joint representation, and Client's consent shall be informed and written. Confidential information shall be protected except to the extent disclosure between jointly represented clients is necessary for the representation or required by applicable professional rules or law.
